title: LicoArc End-to-End Release
goal: Converge every current client plan and every freshly proven blocker into one source-controlled release contract with truthful selected-target releases and a separately gated product-line security claim.
description: Platform-neutral parent plan for product behavior, security, quality, evidence, and exact-artifact contracts consumed by the five platform release children.

title: macOS Release
goal: Produce, authenticate, publish, download, install, launch, and verify each declared macOS artifact through one digest-bound distribution lineage.
description: macOS child of the shared release contract; owns Keychain authorization, target-specific bundles, Developer ID signing, notarization, publication, and launch evidence.

title: Android Release
goal: Produce a deterministic Android arm64 artifact with user-authorized native custody, privacy-safe runtime behavior, physical install and launch proof, and real channel continuity.
description: Android child of the shared release contract; owns Keystore and BiometricPrompt policy, APK lineage, authorized-device evidence, publication, and update continuity.

title: Linux Release
goal: Produce each declared Linux tuple through one artifact path with truthful custody, bounded smoke evidence, publisher identity, installation, launch, and update proof.
description: Linux child of the shared release contract; owns glibc and musl target lineages, Secret Service or memory-only custody, VM evidence, signing, publication, and launch.

title: iOS Release
goal: Replace the declared iOS builder and evidence gaps with a real arm64 client, native custody and FFI proof, signed distribution, physical launch, and Secure Mesh acceptance.
description: iOS child of the shared release contract; remains fail-closed until its builder, LocalAuthentication and Keychain bridge, TestFlight or store lineage, and physical evidence are complete.

title: Windows Release
goal: Produce independently verified Windows x64 and arm64 clients with native authorization, atomic state, signed installers, launch proof, publication, update, and rollback continuity.
description: Windows child of the shared release contract; remains fail-closed until architecture-specific artifacts, PE verification, secure storage, installer lineage, and runtime evidence are complete.
